To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the column density ratios of Ti II to Ca II and Na I to Ca II are constant over a wide range of ISM conditions, that the Ti II to H I column density ratio is also constant, and that the Na I to H I ratio varies over a range of 0.1-0.4.
the Ti and Ca absorption properties in the ISM are constant over all parameters, but the Na absorption is not.
the Ti II and CaII abundances are constant over a large range of Galactic conditions, and that the Ti II/Na I ratio is constant, while the Ca II/Na I and Ti II/NaI ratios are not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interstellar absorption of neutral sodium, singly ionized titanium and singly ionized calcium towards 74 early-type stars in the Milky Way.
the physical conditions of the ISM in the Galactic disc, as traced by the absorption properties of Na, Ti and Ca, in the UV and visible spectral regions.
the properties of Ti and the accuracy of using Na I absorption lines to trace the H I column density of the ISM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Na I column densities do not correlate with the other species and that the Na I and H I column densities do correlate with the Galactic plane distance, but that the Ti II, Ca II and H I column density correlations do not depend on the Galactic plane distance.
the Na I column densities are not good indicators of those for H I.
the Ti and Ca abundances, and hence the Ti and Ca column densities, can be considered as constant in the Galactic disc and hence can be used as reliable indicators of the amount of dust in the ISM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Na I and Ca II absorption properties are very similar.
the Na I column densities are a good indicator of the H I column densities for sightlines where the Na I absorption is saturated.
the column density of Ti II is a reliable tracer of H I and that the column density ratio of Ti II to Ca II can be used as a reliable indicator of the depletion of Ca relative to Ti.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Na I column densities are systematically lower than the corresponding H I column densities.

Na, Ti and Ca occur predominantly in the diffuse ISM.
